examples.ko: 아이들이 놀고 간 거실은 장난감으로 수라장이에요.
examples.en: The living room is a mess of toys after the kids played.

examples.ko: 새벽부터 줄을 선 사람들이 한꺼번에 밀려서 매장 앞이 수라장이 됐어요.
examples.en: The people lined up since dawn all surged forward at once, and the front of the store turned into chaos.
Right after the accident, the scene was sheer chaos.

examples.ko: 시험 전날이면 내 방은 수라장이 따로 없어요.
examples.en: The day before an exam, my room is nothing short of chaos.

examples.ko: 갑자기 불이 꺼지자 극장 안이 수라장으로 변했어요.
examples.en: When the lights suddenly went out, the theater turned into chaos.
You have to stay calm even in the middle of chaos.

explain: 보통은 '아수라장'이라고 많이 말하고, '수라장'은 같은 뜻의 줄인 모양이에요. 말투가 편한 자리에서는 '난장판'이나 '엉망진창'도 써요.
explain_en: People usually say '아수라장', and '수라장' is a shorter form with the same meaning. In casual talk you can also say '난장판' or '엉망진창'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 술수를 써서 계약을 따냈어요.
examples.en: He used a trick to win the contract.
Be careful not to fall for that kind of trick.
He doesn't play fair and only plays tricks.
I noticed the other side's trick and refused right away.
That kind of trick doesn't work for long.
A victory won by tricks isn't joyful.

explain: '꾀'와 달리 남을 속이는 나쁜 느낌이 강해요. '술수를 쓰다', '술수를 부리다', '술수에 넘어가다'처럼 자주 써요. '술책'과 비슷하고 둘 다 좋은 뜻으로는 안 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '꾀' (a clever idea), it strongly suggests deceiving others. It is common in '술수를 쓰다', '술수를 부리다' and '술수에 넘어가다'. It is close to '술책', and neither is used in a good sense.

examples.en: I got scolded for giggling and chatting with a friend in class.
The kids in the back are giggling and chatting.
Stop messing around and get some work done.
What are you two giggling about like that?

examples.ko: 시시덕거리는 소리 때문에 집중할 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't concentrate because of the sound of idle chatter and laughter.
At the team dinner, I joked around with my coworkers.

explain: 별 의미 없는 말로 웃고 떠들 때 쓰고, 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. '수다 떨다'가 이야기를 나누는 것이라면 이 말은 쓸데없이 웃고 장난치는 모습에 가까워요. '시시덕대다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It is used for laughing and chatting about nothing in particular, with a slightly negative feel. While '수다 떨다' is about talking, this word is closer to laughing and goofing around pointlessly. '시시덕대다' has the same meaning.

examples.en: Where do you run around like that every weekend?

examples.ko: 숙제는 안 하고 친구들이랑 밖에서 싸다니기만 해요.
examples.en: He doesn't do his homework and just roams around outside with his friends.

examples.ko: 아들이 하루 종일 싸다니다가 밤늦게 들어왔어요.
examples.en: My son wandered around all day and came home late at night.
It's raining, so where are you running around?

examples.ko: 너무 싸다니지 말고 집에서 좀 쉬세요.
examples.en: Don't go running around so much; rest at home for a bit.
My younger sibling roamed around everywhere throughout the vacation.

explain: 뚜렷한 목적 없이 여기저기 돌아다닌다는 느낌이 있고, 보통 못마땅할 때 써요. 중립적으로 '돌아다니다'라고 하면 되는 곳에 쓰면 말투가 거칠게 들릴 수 있어요. 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It suggests going here and there without a clear purpose, and it usually carries disapproval. Where neutral '돌아다니다' would do, this can sound harsh. Do not use it about someone older or senior.

en: be in an uproar; be in big trouble

examples.en: The child was missing, so the whole house was in an uproar.
If we keep this up and get late, we're really in trouble.
If you lost your wallet, that would be a real mess.
Even in the chaotic atmosphere, the teacher stayed calm.

examples.ko: 엄마가 알면 야단날 테니까 비밀로 해요.
examples.en: If Mom finds out, there'll be trouble, so let's keep it secret.

examples.ko: 서버가 갑자기 멈춰서 회사가 야단나는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: The server suddenly stopped, and I thought the company would be thrown into chaos.

explain: 큰일이 생겨서 소란스럽고 난처해졌을 때 써요. '야단맞다'(꾸중을 듣다), '야단치다'(꾸짖다)와 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리기 쉬우니 구분하세요.
explain_en: Use it when something big happens and things become noisy and troublesome. It sounds similar to '야단맞다' (get scolded) and '야단치다' (scold), so be careful not to mix them up.

examples.en: He threw the window wide open.
Every morning I fling the curtains open and air out the room.

examples.ko: 누가 갑자기 문을 열어젖혀서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Someone suddenly threw the door open and I was startled.

examples.ko: 방문을 열어젖히자 찬 바람이 훅 들어왔어요.
examples.en: When I threw the bedroom door open, a cold wind rushed in.

examples.ko: 동생이 서랍을 열어젖히며 뭘 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is yanking drawers open, looking for something.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 창을 열어젖힌 채 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: I was angry and shouted with the window thrown wide open.

explain: 그냥 '열다'보다 거침없이 확 여는 느낌이 있어요. 문, 창문, 커튼처럼 큰 것을 '활짝' 여는 상황에 잘 어울려요. 조심스럽게 여는 장면에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '열다', it has a bold, sweeping feel of opening something all at once. It fits big things like doors, windows and curtains, often with '활짝'. You wouldn't use it for opening something carefully.

examples.ko: 모기가 귓가에서 왱왱거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: A mosquito was buzzing by my ear, so I couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 밖에서 공사 기계가 하루 종일 왱왱거려요.
examples.en: Construction machines are whirring outside all day long.

examples.ko: 벌 한 마리가 꽃 근처에서 왱왱거리고 있어요.
examples.en: A bee is buzzing around the flowers.

examples.ko: 컴퓨터 팬이 왱왱거리는 소리가 너무 커요.
examples.en: The whirring sound of the computer fan is too loud.
A fly is buzzing around the room.

examples.ko: 머리 위에서 드론이 왱왱거릴 때마다 깜짝 놀라요.
examples.en: I get startled every time a drone buzzes over my head.

explain: 모기, 벌, 파리, 기계처럼 작고 빠르게 움직이는 것이 내는 소리에 써요. '윙윙거리다'와 거의 같게 쓰는 말이에요. '왱왱거리는 소리'처럼 소리를 꾸밀 때도 써요.
explain_en: It describes the sound of small, fast-moving things such as mosquitoes, bees, flies and machines. It is used almost the same as '윙윙거리다'. It can also modify a noun, as in '왱왱거리는 소리' (a buzzing sound).

en: with a clatter; with a thump

examples.en: The child tumbled down the stairs with a clatter.
There was a thumping noise from upstairs.
The shelf collapsed and everything crashed down.
My younger sibling came running in with a thump.
The things on the desk fell with a clatter.

examples.ko: 우당탕 하는 소리에 놀라서 나가 봤어요.
examples.en: The loud crash startled me, so I went out to look.

explain: 물건이 요란하게 부딪치거나 사람이 넘어지고 뛰는 소리를 나타내요. 한 번 '쿵' 하는 소리와 달리 여러 소리가 이어져 시끄러운 느낌이에요. '우당탕 소리가 나다', '우당탕 넘어지다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It imitates the loud sound of things crashing or someone tumbling or running. Unlike a single '쿵', it suggests several noises in a row and a noisy scene. It is used as '우당탕 소리가 나다' or '우당탕 넘어지다'.

en: run about in confusion; run pell-mell

examples.en: At the sudden blackout, the staff ran about in confusion in the lobby.

examples.ko: 지침이 없으니 현장 대응이 우왕좌왕할 수밖에 없지요.
examples.en: With no guidelines, the response on site can't help but be chaotic.

examples.ko: 건물에 불이 나자 사람들이 출구를 찾지 못해 우왕좌왕하며 헤맸어요.
examples.en: When the building caught fire, people couldn't find the exit and wandered around in confusion.

examples.ko: 시험 시간이 부족해서 우왕좌왕하다가 답을 못 썼어요.
examples.en: I ran out of time on the test, flustered, and couldn't write my answers.
Don't panic; calmly do it in order.

examples.ko: 정책이 자꾸 바뀌어서 학교도 우왕좌왕하고 있어요.
examples.en: Policies keep changing, so the schools are also in confusion.

explain: 사람이나 조직이 혼란스러워서 방향을 못 잡을 때 써요. '허둥지둥'은 급해서 서두르는 느낌이고, '우왕좌왕'은 갈피를 못 잡고 이리저리 움직이는 느낌이에요. '갈팡질팡'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It is used when people or organizations are confused and can't find a direction. '허둥지둥' feels like rushing in a hurry, while '우왕좌왕' feels like moving this way and that without direction. '갈팡질팡' is used similarly.

examples.en: A mosquito is buzzing around my ear.
The fridge hums all night.
Bees are gathered buzzing in the flower field.
The fan whirs around and it's noisy.

examples.ko: 드론이 머리 위에서 윙윙 날고 있어요.
examples.en: A drone is whizzing above my head.

examples.ko: 귀에서 윙윙 소리가 나서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My ears were ringing, so I went to the hospital.

explain: 벌, 모기, 기계가 빠르게 돌 때 나는 낮고 계속되는 소리예요. 보통 '윙윙 소리가 나다', '윙윙거리다'로 써요. 귀에서 나는 소리에도 쓰는데, 몸이 안 좋을 때 쓰는 말이니 병원 이야기와 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a low, continuous sound made by bees, mosquitoes or fast-spinning machines. It is used as '윙윙 소리가 나다' or '윙윙거리다'. It also describes ringing in the ears, so it often shows up in talk about health.

examples.en: I knocked my friend down while playing around.
The child running toward me almost knocked me over.
In ssireum, you win if you knock your opponent down.
The puppy jumped on Grandma and knocked her over.
I didn't mean to knock you down.

examples.ko: 바닥에 놓인 가방이 사람을 자빠뜨릴 수도 있어요.
examples.en: A bag left on the floor can trip someone.

explain: '넘어뜨리다'와 뜻은 같지만 더 거칠고 구어적인 느낌이에요. 스스로 넘어지는 '자빠지다'와 짝이라서, 남을 넘어지게 할 때 '자빠뜨리다'를 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '넘어뜨리다' but sounds rougher and more colloquial. It pairs with '자빠지다' (to fall over by oneself); use '자빠뜨리다' when you make someone else fall.

examples.en: The kids chatter away in the classroom all day.

examples.ko: 새들이 아침마다 창문 밖에서 재잘대서 일찍 깨요.
examples.en: Birds twitter outside my window every morning, so I wake up early.

examples.ko: 동생은 학교에서 있었던 일을 신나게 재잘댔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling excitedly chattered about what happened at school.

examples.ko: 뒷자리 친구들이 수업 시간에 재잘대면 선생님이 주의를 주세요.
examples.en: If the friends in the back chatter during class, the teacher warns them.

examples.ko: 딸이 차 안에서 쉬지 않고 재잘대는 소리가 귀여워요.
examples.en: The sound of my daughter chattering nonstop in the car is cute.

examples.ko: 조카는 친해지면 쉬지 않고 재잘대기 시작해요.
examples.en: Once my nephew gets comfortable, he starts chattering nonstop.

explain: 아이나 새처럼 작은 목소리로 빠르게 계속 말하는 모습에 어울리고, 귀엽게 느끼는 뉘앙스가 있어요. 같은 뜻으로 '재잘거리다'도 써요. 어른이 큰 소리로 시끄럽게 말하면 '떠들다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It suits children or birds talking quickly and continuously in small voices, often with a cute feel. '재잘거리다' means the same thing. For adults being loud, '떠들다' sounds more natural.

en: braking; a brake or check on something

examples.en: The driver suddenly hit the brakes.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 제동 거리가 길어져요.
examples.en: On rainy days, the braking distance gets longer.

examples.ko: 자전거의 제동이 잘 안 돼서 위험했어요.
examples.en: The bike's brakes didn't work well, so it was dangerous.
The new rule put the brakes on the business.

examples.ko: 정부의 발표로 가격 상승에 제동이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The government announcement put the brakes on rising prices.
The train stopped because of a problem with the braking system.

explain: 제동은 차나 기계를 멈추게 하는 일을 말해요. 자동차 브레이크를 눌러 속도를 줄일 때 쓰고, 계획이나 흐름을 막는다는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '브레이크를 밟다'가 더 흔해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 멈추는 게 아니라 어떤 일이 더 진행되지 못하게 막을 때 써요. 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not for stopping a car but for holding back a trend or plan. Very common in news.

explain_en: 제동 is the act of stopping or slowing a vehicle or machine. It is also used figuratively for stopping a plan or trend. In everyday speech Koreans more often say 브레이크를 밟다 (step on the brake).

examples.en: My aim was accurate, so I hit it in one go.
When shooting a bow, I focus on aiming.
I practiced aiming every day.
I aimed wrong, so the arrow missed.

examples.ko: 조준은 끝났고 이제 쏘기만 하면 돼요.
examples.en: The aiming is done, and now I just have to shoot.

examples.ko: 조준의 정확도를 높이는 연습 게임이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a practice game that improves aiming accuracy.

explain: '조준을 하다', '조준이 정확하다'처럼 활, 물총, 게임에서 자주 들려요. 일상에서는 '겨냥'이라는 말도 비슷하게 쓰여요. '목표를 조준하다'처럼 비유로 노리는 대상을 정할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Heard in archery, water guns, and games, as in '조준을 하다' and '조준이 정확하다'. The similar word '겨냥' is also used in daily life. It also works figuratively for picking a target, as in '목표를 조준하다'.

examples.en: The game was stopped because of the rain.
The street has been quiet since the construction was halted.
Elevator service stops when the power goes out.
The service is scheduled to be suspended for a while.

examples.ko: 회사 전산망이 갑자기 중지되어서 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: The company network was suddenly shut down, so I could not work.

examples.ko: 사고 때문에 지하철 운행이 중지되었다고 해요.
examples.en: I heard subway service was suspended because of an accident.

explain: 하던 일이 어떤 이유로 멈출 때 써요. 누가 일부러 멈추면 '중지하다', 일이 저절로 또는 사정 때문에 멈추면 '중지되다'예요. 뉴스와 안내문에서는 '중단되다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when something that was going on stops for some reason. When someone stops it on purpose, it is '중지하다'; when it stops by circumstance, it is '중지되다'. In news and notices, '중단되다' is also commonly used with the same meaning.

examples.en: The child keeps whining for me to buy it.
Don't whine, try saying it in words.
It's tiring because of my friend who whines about being tired.
My younger sibling has been whining since morning, so it's noisy.
You shouldn't whine even after you become an adult.

examples.ko: 징징거릴 시간에 하나라도 더 해 봐요.
examples.en: Instead of whining, try doing one more thing.

explain: '징징대다'와 같은 뜻으로, 우는소리를 내며 보채거나 불평하는 모습을 말해요. 아이에게 많이 쓰지만 어른이 힘들다고 계속 불평할 때도 쓰는데, 그때는 조금 핀잔하는 말투예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '징징대다', describing fussing or complaining in a crying tone. It is used a lot for children, but also for adults who keep complaining about hardship, in which case it sounds a bit scolding.

en: traditional folk song; saying the same thing over and over (nagging)

examples.en: I heard one folk song at the performance.

examples.ko: 동생은 하루 종일 용돈 타령만 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling goes on and on about allowance all day long.
My friend teased me, asking if I was going on about graduation again.

examples.ko: 이 지역에는 흥겨운 타령이 많이 전해져요.
examples.en: Many lively folk songs are handed down in this region.

examples.ko: 맨날 불평 타령을 해도 달라지는 것은 없어요.
examples.en: Nothing changes no matter how often you keep complaining.

examples.ko: 아이가 새 장난감 타령에 들어가면 끝이 없어요.
examples.en: Once the child starts going on about a new toy, it never ends.

explain: 원래는 민요나 판소리처럼 우리나라 전통 노래의 한 종류예요. 요즘은 '돈 타령', '취직 타령'처럼 같은 말을 계속 반복하며 조른다는 쓰임으로 더 많이 써요. 이 쓰임에는 조금 귀찮아하는 느낌이 들어 있어요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling keeps going on about a new phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 것을 계속 말하거나 졸라서 듣는 사람이 지칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone keeps talking about or begging for the same thing until the listener is worn out.

explain_en: It originally names a type of traditional Korean song, like folk songs or pansori. Today it is used more often, as in 돈 타령 or 취직 타령, for repeating the same thing over and over, nagging. This usage carries a slightly annoyed feel.

examples.en: Grandfather is scooping water out of the well.

examples.ko: 배 안에 고인 물을 빨리 퍼내야 해요.
examples.en: We have to bail out the water in the boat quickly.
I shoveled out the snow and made a path.

examples.ko: 엄마가 밥솥에서 밥을 한 그릇 퍼냈어요.
examples.en: Mom scooped a bowl of rice out of the rice cooker.
Please ladle out the soup with the big ladle.

examples.ko: 연못의 흙탕물을 다 퍼내면 물고기가 보여요.
examples.en: If you scoop out all the muddy water from the pond, you can see the fish.

explain: '푸다'에 '내다'가 붙어서 안에 있는 것을 떠서 밖으로 빼내는 느낌이 강해요. '푸다'는 '퍼요'처럼 바뀌지만 '퍼내다'는 '퍼내요'로 규칙적으로 써요. 반대로 떠서 안에 넣을 때는 '퍼 담다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It combines '푸다' (to scoop) with '내다', so it stresses taking something out from inside. '푸다' changes to '퍼요', but '퍼내다' is regular: '퍼내요'. To scoop something into a container, say '퍼 담다'.

examples.ko: 화가 난 손님이 가게에서 행패를 부려서 경찰이 왔어요.
examples.en: An angry customer made a scene in the shop, so the police came.
When the rowdy behavior got worse, the neighbors reported it to the police.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 행패를 더는 참을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't put up with that person's outrageous behavior any longer.

examples.ko: 그런 행패에도 직원들은 끝까지 친절하게 대했어요.
examples.en: Despite such rude behavior, the staff stayed kind to the end.

examples.ko: 손님의 행패로 가게가 잠시 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: The shop closed for a while because of a customer's disorderly behavior.

examples.ko: 동생이 마트에서 행패를 부려서 정말 창피했어요.
examples.en: My younger brother threw a fit at the supermarket, and I was so embarrassed.

explain: '행패를 부리다'가 가장 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 소리를 지르거나 물건을 던지는 등 남에게 피해를 주는 거친 행동을 말해요. 그런 일을 겪은 쪽은 '행패를 당하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The most common pairing is '행패를 부리다' (to make a scene / act outrageously). It refers to rough behavior such as yelling or throwing things that bothers others. The person on the receiving end says '행패를 당하다'.

examples.en: The kids walked freely around the park and played happily.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 편한 옷차림으로 거리를 활보했어요.
examples.en: The singer strode down the street in casual clothes.
It's a neighborhood where you can safely stroll the night streets alone.

examples.ko: 강아지가 집 안을 마음껏 활보하고 있어요.
examples.en: The puppy is roaming around the house as it pleases.

examples.ko: 한복을 입고 시내를 활보하는 외국인들이 많아졌어요.
examples.en: More foreigners now stroll around downtown in hanbok.

examples.ko: 비가 그치자 고양이가 마당을 활보하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Once the rain stopped, the cat began to prowl around the yard.

explain: 어깨를 펴고 거침없이 당당하게 걷는 모습을 말해요. 그냥 '걷다'보다 거리낌 없고 자신 있는 느낌이 있어요. 사람뿐 아니라 동물에게도 쓰고, 잘못한 사람이 아무렇지 않게 다닐 때 비판하는 말로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes walking boldly with shoulders back and no hesitation. Compared with plain '걷다', it feels confident and unrestrained. It is used for animals too, and also as criticism when someone who did wrong moves around as if nothing happened.

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 걸을 때 몸이 휘청거려요.
examples.en: I'm so tired that my body wobbles when I walk.
The wind was strong, so the bicycle wobbled.

examples.ko: 무거운 짐을 들다가 휘청거리는 바람에 넘어질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I staggered while carrying a heavy load and almost fell.
My legs went weak and I walked unsteadily.

examples.ko: 경기가 나빠서 그 회사가 휘청거리고 있어요.
examples.en: The economy is bad and that company is wobbling.

examples.ko: 밥을 못 먹었더니 어지러워서 휘청거릴 것 같아요.
examples.en: I haven't eaten and feel dizzy, like I might stagger.

explain: '흔들리다'와 비슷하지만 '휘청거리다'는 몸이나 길쭉한 물건이 힘없이 이리저리 기우는 모습에 써요. 사람이 불안하게 걷는 모습에는 '비틀거리다'도 써요. 회사나 경제가 흔들릴 때도 비유로 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is like '흔들리다', but '휘청거리다' describes a body or a long, thin object leaning weakly from side to side. For a person walking unsteadily, '비틀거리다' is also used. It can also be used figuratively when a company or the economy is shaky.

examples.ko: 옆자리 사람이 제 휴대폰을 힐끔 봤어요.
examples.en: The person next to me glanced at my phone.
He glanced at his watch and then stood up.
The child stole a glance to check his mom's mood.
People passing by glanced at us.
Why do you keep glancing at me?

examples.ko: 그녀는 뒤를 힐끔 돌아보고 빨리 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: She glanced back and walked away quickly.

explain: '힐끗'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 몰래 또는 빠르게 한 번 보는 느낌이라서 오래 바라보는 '빤히'와 반대예요. 보통 '힐끔 보다, 쳐다보다, 돌아보다'로 쓰고, 여러 번 반복하면 '힐끔힐끔'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '힐끗'. It gives the feeling of looking once, quickly or secretly, so it is the opposite of '빤히' (staring). It usually goes with '보다, 쳐다보다, 돌아보다', and repeated glances are '힐끔힐끔'.
